code.why: The descriptor's credentialDoor at a World's boot: the runtime asks the api-token door for its default acme account, which this makes. The life and the examples sign up Tidewater themselves, so only a World's boot calls it.

The host factory is exercised by conformance standalone and life-over-HTTP; the in-memory life walker drives fetch directly. Architecture Coverage explicitly permits the host process around fetch to be recorded.

The descriptor's credentialDoor asked again when a World resumes: the runtime boots the World and asks the api-token door for its default acme account's token a second time, and the token issued at the first boot is answered again. The life and the examples never boot a World, so only a resumed World reaches it (the customer entry's stop and resume).
